title: Fsck
description: Result of `rebar fsck --output json`: {issues, fixed, issue_count}. Each issue has a `kind` (corrupt, corrupt_create, missing_create, snapshot_inconsistent, orphan_event, warn, push_pending, …) and a detail; per-ticket kinds also carry ticket_id (and filename). `fixed` lists auto-repaired items. Exit 0 = clean, 1 = issues (unchanged). The optional `returncode` carries a COMPLETED run's exit code as data, and `mode` discriminates a scan result from a `fsck-recover` result, whose plain-English narrative is carried verbatim in `report` (that command emits no KIND: lines and has no --output json). All three are optional and absent from the CLI's own `--output json` payload, which is always a scan.

returncode.description: Exit code of the COMPLETED run, carried as data: 0 = clean, 1 = issues found (scan) or attempted-but-nothing-recovered (recover). Emitted by the structured surfaces (library `fsck_report()`, MCP `fsck`); absent from the CLI's `--output json`.

mode.description: Which operation produced this result. 'scan' = the integrity scan, where issues/fixed/issue_count are meaningful. 'recover' = the destructive fsck-recover repair, which produces ACTIONS rather than findings, so issues/fixed are empty, issue_count is 0, and the narrative is in `report`.

report.description: The verbatim fsck-recover narrative when mode='recover'. Null for a scan, whose report IS the structured issues array.
